instructions: 39 questions, 80 marks, 3 hours. Same sections, question types, marks and internal choices as the CBSE Sample Question Paper 2026-27.
Section A is Biology, Section B Chemistry, Section C Physics, as in the CBSE paper. Draw diagrams on paper where asked.
Objective questions (MCQ, assertion-reason, numeric) are marked automatically.
Written answers: write on paper (or type in the box). After you submit, compare with the model answer and award your own marks point by point, the way a board examiner uses the marking scheme.

The timer runs for the full 3 hours as a guide; nothing is cut off. Time spent in each section is shown in your report.

ch10.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.question: In plants, food made in the leaves is transported to other parts through the:
questions.explanation: Translocation of food (sucrose) takes place in phloem; xylem carries water and minerals.

questions.question: The respiratory pigment in human blood that carries oxygen is:
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells has a high affinity for oxygen.

questions.question: Insulin, which regulates blood sugar, is secreted by the:
questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the pancreas; its deficiency causes diabetes.

questions.question: The growth of a pollen tube towards the ovule is an example of:
questions.explanation: The pollen tube grows in response to chemicals: chemotropism.

questions.question: Which organism commonly reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Hydra forms buds; Planaria regenerates, Amoeba shows binary fission, Plasmodium multiple fission.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in a human sperm or egg cell is:
questions.explanation: Gametes have half the 46 chromosomes of body cells.

questions.question: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, the grass traps 10,000 J. The energy available to the snake is about:
questions.explanation: About 10% passes on at each step: 10,000 → 1,000 → 100 → 10 J.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: Adrenaline is secreted by the thyroid gland.
questions.reason: Adrenaline prepares the body to deal with an emergency, for example by increasing the heart rate.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands, so A is false; R correctly describes what adrenaline does.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: The concentration of pesticides such as DDT is highest in the top carnivores of a food chain.
questions.reason: Non-biodegradable chemicals are not broken down and accumulate progressively at each trophic level.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both true; progressive accumulation (biological magnification) is the reason top carnivores carry the most.

questions.question: Name the plant hormone that (i) inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves, (ii) helps a shoot bend towards light. Explain how the shoot bends.
questions.model_answer:
(i) Abscisic acid. (ii) Auxin.
Auxin is made at the shoot tip. When light falls from one side, auxin diffuses to the shaded side, where cells grow longer, so the shoot bends towards the light.

rubric.p: Auxin moves to the shaded side; those cells elongate, shoot bends to light

alts.question: What is the importance of DNA copying in reproduction?
alts.model_answer:
DNA carries the information for making proteins, which decides the body design. Copying DNA lets the basic body design pass on to the offspring.
The copying is not perfectly accurate; the small variations that arise help species survive changing conditions over time.

rubric.p: Passes body design / information to offspring
Copying errors give variations useful for survival

alts.label: A

alts.question: Distinguish between unisexual and bisexual flowers with one example of each.
alts.model_answer:
Unisexual flowers contain either stamens or a pistil (e.g. papaya, watermelon).
Bisexual flowers contain both stamens and a pistil (e.g. hibiscus, mustard).
alts.label: B

questions.question: How are the lungs designed in human beings to maximise the area for the exchange of gases?
questions.model_answer: Inside the lungs the air passages divide into smaller and smaller tubes ending in balloon-like alveoli. Alveoli provide a very large surface for gas exchange, and their walls carry an extensive network of blood vessels, so oxygen diffuses into the blood and CO₂ out of it.

rubric.p: Branching tubes ending in alveoli give a huge surface area
Thin walls with dense blood capillaries for exchange

questions.question: Describe how a nephron forms urine.
questions.model_answer:
Blood enters the glomerulus, a cluster of capillaries inside Bowman's capsule, where it is filtered: water, glucose, amino acids, salts and nitrogenous wastes such as urea pass into the tubule.
As the filtrate moves along the tubule, useful substances (glucose, amino acids, salts and a major amount of water) are selectively reabsorbed into the blood.
The remaining fluid, urine, passes to the collecting duct, then through the ureter to the urinary bladder.

rubric.p: Selective reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, salts, water
Urine to collecting duct → ureter → bladder

questions.question: What are trophic levels? Give an example of a food chain with four trophic levels. Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels?
questions.model_answer:
Trophic levels are the steps of a food chain at which energy is transferred (producers, herbivores, carnivores…).
Example: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake.
Only about 10% of energy passes to the next level and the rest is lost (mostly as heat), so after four or five levels too little energy is left to support another level.

questions.stem: In an experiment, pea plants with violet flowers (VV) were crossed with plants with white flowers (vv). The F₁ plants were self-pollinated.

parts.question: The flowers of all F₁ plants are:
parts.explanation: Violet is dominant; F₁ is Vv. There is no blending.

parts.question: The genotypic ratio in F₂ is:
parts.explanation: Vv × Vv gives VV, Vv, Vv, vv.

alts.question: If 800 F₂ plants are obtained, how many would have white flowers? Show your working.
alts.model_answer: White flowers need vv, which is 1/4 of F₂. 1/4 × 800 = 200 plants.
alts.label: A

alts.question: How can you find out whether an F₂ violet-flowered plant is VV or Vv?
alts.model_answer: Cross it with a white-flowered (vv) plant. If all offspring are violet, the plant is VV; if about half are white, it is Vv.

rubric.p: All violet → VV; some white → Vv

alts.label: B

alts.question: Describe sexual reproduction in a flowering plant: pollination, growth of the pollen tube, fertilisation and the changes after fertilisation.
alts.model_answer:
Pollination: pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma (self- or cross-pollination by wind, water or animals).
The pollen grain grows a pollen tube through the style to reach the ovule in the ovary.
Fertilisation: the male germ-cell fuses with the female germ-cell (egg) in the ovule, forming a zygote.
After fertilisation the zygote divides to form the embryo, the ovule becomes the seed with a tough coat, the ovary ripens into the fruit, and petals, sepals, stamens, style and stigma usually shrivel and fall off.

rubric.p: Ovary → fruit; other parts fall off

alts.label: A

alts.question: Describe the digestion of food along the human alimentary canal: mouth, stomach, small intestine and large intestine.
alts.model_answer:
Mouth: teeth break food; saliva has salivary amylase, which breaks starch into sugar.
Stomach: gastric glands release hydrochloric acid (acidic medium, kills germs), pepsin (digests proteins) and mucus (protects the lining).
Small intestine: bile from the liver emulsifies fats and makes the medium alkaline; pancreatic juice has trypsin (proteins) and lipase (fats); intestinal juice completes digestion. Villi absorb digested food into the blood.
Large intestine: absorbs excess water; the rest is removed through the anus.
alts.label: B

questions.question: When water is electrolysed, the ratio of the volumes of hydrogen and oxygen collected is:
questions.explanation: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂: twice as much hydrogen by volume.

questions.question: On heating lead nitrate, the brown fumes given off are of:
questions.explanation: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂; NO₂ is brown.

questions.question: Tooth decay starts when the pH in the mouth falls below:
questions.explanation: Enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) corrodes below pH 5.5.

questions.question: Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide solution on heating. The gas evolved is:
questions.explanation: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂.

questions.question: An element burns to form an oxide whose solution turns blue litmus red. The element is most likely:
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides are acidic; SO₂ dissolves to give an acidic solution.

questions.question: The general formula of alkynes is:
questions.explanation: Alkynes have a triple bond: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (e.g. C₂H₂).

questions.question: Ethanol is converted into ethanoic acid by alkaline potassium permanganate. This reaction is an example of:
questions.explanation: Alkaline KMnO₄ is an oxidising agent: it adds oxygen to ethanol.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: Concentrated sulphuric acid should be diluted by adding the acid slowly to water, with constant stirring.
questions.reason: Dissolving an acid in water is a highly exothermic process.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Adding water to concentrated acid can make the mixture splash and the glass break from local heating; R is the reason.

questions.question: How is bleaching powder prepared? Write the equation and give two uses.
questions.model_answer:
Chlorine is passed over dry slaked lime: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.
Uses (any two): bleaching cotton and linen, and wood pulp; disinfecting drinking water; as an oxidising agent in industry.

alts.question: What is corrosion? Name the coating formed on copper and on silver when they corrode. Give two methods to prevent rusting of iron.
alts.model_answer:
Corrosion: a metal is slowly attacked by substances around it such as moisture and gases, and its surface wears away.
Copper gets a green coat of basic copper carbonate; silver turns black with silver sulphide.
Prevent rusting by painting, oiling or greasing, galvanising (zinc coating), chrome plating, anodising or making alloys (e.g. stainless steel). Any two.

rubric.p: Copper: green basic copper carbonate; silver: black silver sulphide

alts.label: A

alts.question: Write balanced equations for the reaction of (a) sodium with cold water, (b) magnesium with hot water, (c) aluminium with steam. Why is sodium stored under kerosene?
alts.model_answer:
(a) 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ + heat.
(b) Mg + 2H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ + H₂.
(c) 2Al + 3H₂O → Al₂O₃ + 3H₂.
Sodium reacts so vigorously with oxygen and moisture that it can catch fire, so it is kept under kerosene.
alts.label: B

questions.question:
Balance the following and name the type of each reaction:
(a) Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ (steam)
(b) Pb(NO₃)₂ + KI → PbI₂ + KNO₃
(c) CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (on heating)
questions.model_answer:
(a) 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂ (redox: iron oxidised).
(b) Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃: double displacement (yellow precipitate of PbI₂).
(c) CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂: thermal decomposition.

questions.stem: Vinegar is a 5–8% solution of a compound X (C₂H₄O₂) in water. Pure X freezes in cold weather. X reacts with ethanol in the presence of an acid to give a sweet-smelling compound.

parts.question: The functional group in X is:
X reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The gas is:

alts.question: Write the equation for the reaction of X with ethanol and give one use of the product.
alts.model_answer:
CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (in the presence of an acid catalyst): ethyl ethanoate, an ester.
Use: in perfumes and flavouring agents (esters with alkali give soap: saponification).
alts.label: A

alts.question: Why is pure X called glacial acetic acid? Is X a strong or a weak acid?
alts.model_answer:
Pure ethanoic acid has a melting point of 290 K, so it often freezes in cold climates, looking like ice: hence 'glacial'.
It is a weak acid (it ionises only partly in water).
alts.label: B

alts.question: (a) Give two reasons why carbon forms a very large number of compounds. (b) Explain why carbon forms covalent bonds rather than ions. (c) Describe the bonding in ethane (C₂H₆) using electron dots, and state why covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity.
alts.model_answer:
(a) Catenation: carbon links with other carbon atoms to form long chains, branches and rings. Tetravalency: carbon has four valence electrons and bonds with four other atoms (C, H, O, N, S, Cl…). Strong C–C and C–H bonds (small atom) make the compounds stable.
(b) Gaining or losing four electrons would need too much energy, so carbon shares its valence electrons.
(c) Each carbon shares one pair with the other carbon and one pair with each of three hydrogens (7 shared pairs in all).
Covalent compounds have no free ions, so they are poor conductors.

rubric.p: Ethane dot structure: one C–C and six C–H shared pairs

alts.label: A

alts.question: Explain, with equations, how mercury is obtained from its sulphide ore (cinnabar, HgS). Then describe the electrolytic refining of copper.
alts.model_answer:
Mercury is low in the reactivity series, so heating alone works. Roasting: 2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂. Further heating reduces the oxide: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂.
Electrolytic refining: impure copper is the anode, a thin strip of pure copper the cathode, and acidified copper sulphate solution the electrolyte. On passing current, copper dissolves from the anode into the solution and pure copper deposits on the cathode; insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud.

rubric.p: CuSO₄ electrolyte and what happens on passing current

alts.label: B

questions.question: The power of a lens of focal length −50 cm is:
questions.explanation: P = 1/f (in m) = 1/(−0.5) = −2 D: a concave lens.

questions.question: The magnification produced by a plane mirror is:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms an erect image of the same size.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.assertion: The sky appears dark to an astronaut in space.
questions.reason: There is no atmosphere in space to scatter sunlight.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Scattering by the atmosphere makes the sky look blue; without an atmosphere there is no scattering, so the sky looks dark.

questions.question: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. What does this mean? Find the speed of light in glass (speed in air = 3 × 10⁸ m/s).
questions.model_answer:
n = speed of light in air / speed of light in glass = 1.5: light travels 1.5 times faster in air than in glass.
v = c/n = 3 × 10⁸ / 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s.

alts.question: State Ohm's law. A bulb draws a current of 0.5 A from a 220 V supply. Find its resistance.
alts.model_answer:
At constant temperature, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends (V = IR).
R = V/I = 220/0.5 = 440 Ω.
alts.label: A

alts.question: Give two properties of magnetic field lines. Why do two field lines never intersect?
alts.model_answer:
Field lines emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole (closed curves); they are closer where the field is stronger.
If two lines crossed, the compass needle at that point would point in two directions at once, which is impossible.
alts.label: B

questions.question: What is hypermetropia? State two possible causes and how it is corrected.
questions.model_answer:
Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): a person sees distant objects clearly but not nearby ones; the near point is farther than 25 cm and the image of a near object forms behind the retina.
Causes: the focal length of the eye lens is too long, or the eyeball has become too small.
Correction: a convex lens of suitable power, which gives extra focusing.

rubric.p: Definition (near point beyond 25 cm, image behind retina)

questions.question:
A copper wire is 2 m long with an area of cross-section 1.7 × 10⁻⁶ m². The resistivity of copper is 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m.
(a) Find its resistance. (b) How will the resistance change if the length is halved? (c) How will it change if the diameter is doubled?
questions.model_answer:
(a) R = ρl/A = (1.7 × 10⁻⁸ × 2)/(1.7 × 10⁻⁶) = 0.02 Ω.
(b) R ∝ l, so it is halved (0.01 Ω).
(c) Doubling the diameter makes the area four times, so R becomes one-fourth (0.005 Ω).

questions.topic: Field due to a circular loop
questions.question: Describe the magnetic field pattern of a current-carrying circular loop. How does the field at the centre change if (a) the current is increased, (b) the coil has n turns?
questions.model_answer:
Near the wire, the field lines are concentric circles; as we move towards the centre the arcs become larger, and at the centre the lines are nearly straight and perpendicular to the plane of the loop.
(a) The field increases with current.
(b) With n turns the fields add up, so the field becomes n times that of a single turn.

rubric.p: Pattern: circles near wire, straight at centre
n turns → n times the field

questions.stem: In the school lab, a student uses a convex lens of focal length 12 cm and places a candle at different distances from it.

parts.topic: Image formation by a convex lens
parts.question: When the candle is 24 cm from the lens, the image is:
options: real, inverted, same size, 24 cm behind the lens
parts.explanation: 24 cm = 2F, so the image is at 2F on the other side, same size.

parts.topic: Image formation by a convex lens
parts.question: To get a virtual, erect and magnified image, the candle must be placed:
options: between the lens and its focus
parts.explanation: Only an object within F gives a virtual, erect, magnified image (magnifying glass).

alts.question: Find the power of this lens.
alts.label: A

alts.question: Find the image distance when the candle is 36 cm from the lens.
alts.model_answer: u = −36 cm, f = +12 cm. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/12 − 1/36 = 2/36, so v = +18 cm (real image behind the lens).
alts.label: B

alts.question: State Joule's law of heating. Find the heat produced in 5 minutes in a 4 Ω resistor carrying a current of 2 A. Give two applications of the heating effect and explain why the filament of a bulb is made of tungsten.
alts.model_answer:
Joule's law: heat produced H = I²Rt; heat is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time for which current flows.
H = 2² × 4 × 300 = 4800 J.
Applications: electric iron, toaster, heater, kettle, fuse, electric bulb (any two).
Tungsten has a very high melting point (3380 °C), so it can glow white-hot without melting.
alts.label: A

alts.question: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected to a 12 V source. Find the equivalent resistance and the current drawn when they are connected (a) in series, (b) in parallel. Give two reasons why household appliances are connected in parallel.
alts.model_answer:
(a) Series: R = 18 Ω, I = 12/18 = 0.67 A (approx.).
(b) Parallel: 1/R = 3/6, R = 2 Ω, I = 12/2 = 6 A.
Parallel: each appliance gets the full supply voltage; each can be switched on or off independently, and if one fails the others keep working; the total resistance is less.
alts.label: B
